wrapup.introPost: , the system injects this "wrap-up prompt" to run one final round: first write back any identified-but-unsaved content, then output a summary (to avoid an abrupt ending). Leave empty to use the built-in default.

tt.introRest: (a separate set from the per-run wrap-up above): injected when the entire task reaches its timeout limit and is about to end. Its semantics are often the opposite of per-run (e.g. planner: per-run says "don't stop, keep planning," while task-timeout says "stop now, make the final judgment"). Leave empty to use the built-in default.

pool.title: LLM failover
pool.desc: When on, if the active profile runs out of credit / has a bad key / bad network, tasks automatically switch to the next configured profile — one 402 no longer stalls everything. Needs ≥2 profiles with API keys.
pool.needTwo: Failover needs at least 2 profiles with API keys. Add another profile below first.

roles.title: Role → LLM (division of labor)
roles.desc: Assign an LLM per role; by default all follow the global active profile (use the strongest model your environment allows — stronger agents, especially the worker, mine better). Override a role only when it is access-restricted, or needs a specific / longer-output model (e.g. report enrichment). Agents coordinate via the exploration graph, so mixing models does not hurt coordination.

traffic.title: Traffic Capture
traffic.desc1: When enabled, all Agent HTTP traffic is fully persisted through the recording proxy, and the traffic_search / traffic_get tools plus proxy configuration are injected into Agents (the prompt includes proxy instructions).
traffic.desc2: When off (default), no traffic is recorded: Agents will not receive the proxy configuration or traffic tools, and the prompt does not include any proxy-related content. Switching rebuilds Agents to take effect immediately.
traffic.on: Enabled · recording traffic and injecting proxy
traffic.off: Disabled · not recording, not injecting proxy

webSearch.title: Web Search
webSearch.desc1: This is the master switch + source configuration for web search. Once enabled, you can choose whether to turn on web_search individually in each Agent's configuration (returns only title/link/summary, does not fetch the body; fetching is handled by WebFetch). Web search does not go through the recording proxy and is independent of traffic capture.
webSearch.desc2: Sources include DuckDuckGo (ddgs) (no key required), Brave (free tier) (requires a Brave API Key), or Tavily (requires a Tavily API Key). When the master switch is off, each Agent's web search toggle is unavailable.
webSearch.on: Master switch on · can be enabled individually per Agent
webSearch.off: Disabled · Agents cannot enable web search
webSearch.braveNeedsKey: Brave selected but no key configured yet —— the search tool will not be enabled until you save a key.
webSearch.braveHint: Free tier ~2,000 queries/month. Get a key at https://brave.com/search/api/.
webSearch.tavilyNeedsKey: Tavily selected but no key configured yet —— the search tool will not be enabled until you save a key.
webSearch.tavilyHint: Register and get an API Key at https://tavily.com.
webSearch.proxyHint: A dedicated egress proxy used only to reach search endpoints (VPN/SOCKS, etc.). Unrelated to the MITM proxy that records traffic; used to connect when the network is otherwise unreachable.
webSearch.testHint: Run a real search for "test" with the current configuration (source + proxy + key) to verify it works.
